translation: Pallavi (Chorus): For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot; draped in a saree of many colours, she has mounted the chariot. For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot; draped in a saree of many colours, she has mounted the chariot. (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot; draped in a saree of many colours, she has mounted the chariot)

Verse 1: With turmeric and kumkum in their hands, the young women have come; dressed in silk sarees, the young women have come; with turmeric and kumkum in their hands, the young women have come; dressed in silk sarees, the young women have come; they have come now to worship Yellamma; they have come to fulfil their vows to the great Mother. (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot...)

Verse 2: Carrying the bonam on their heads, the devotees have come; they have offered naivedyam to the great Mother; carrying the bonam on their heads, the devotees have come; they have offered naivedyam to the great Mother; strike up the beat with the sound of the dappu drums; everyone, bow down to Mother Yellamma. (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot...)

Verse 3: Lay neem branches and put up a pandal; place garlands of jasmine around her neck; lay neem branches and put up a pandal; place garlands of jasmine around her neck; they prayed, 'Keep us safe and well, Mother'; they vowed, 'Bless us, Mother'. (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot...)

Verse 4: They brought water in a golden pot; they have now given the Mother her bath; they brought water in a golden pot; they have now given the Mother her bath; Yellamma of the seven villages, you are our sovereign; come and protect all the people of our village, Mother. (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot; draped in a saree of many colours, she has mounted the chariot) (For Yellamma of the glittering gems they have decked out a chariot; draped in a saree of many colours, she has mounted the chariot)
summaryEn:
A devotional song describing a village festival for Yellamma, the mother goddess widely worshipped across Telangana. The goddess, called 'Yellamma of the glittering gems', is dressed in a colourful saree and placed on a decorated chariot for the procession. Young women arrive in silk sarees carrying turmeric and kumkum to worship her and fulfil their vows (mokkulu). Devotees carry the bonam — a pot of cooked food offering — on their heads, in the manner of the Bonalu festival, and present naivedyam while the dappu drums beat out the rhythm.

The song also records the details of the ritual space. A pandal (canopy) is built with neem branches, a plant closely linked with the village goddess, and the image is adorned with jasmine garlands and bathed with water from a golden pot. Throughout, the worshippers ask the Mother to keep them 'sallaga' — cool, safe and well — and to bless them. The last verse hails her as 'Yellamma of the seven villages' and sovereign protector, asking her to guard everyone in the village. The mix of descriptive lines and calls to action (beat the drums, bow down, build the pandal) suggests a song sung by the crowd as part of the festival itself.

తెలంగాణ అంతటా విస్తృతంగా కొలిచే గ్రామదేవత ఎల్లమ్మ జాతరను వర్ణించే భక్తి గీతం ఇది. పండుగను కళ్లకు కట్టినట్టు వివరిస్తూ సాగుతుంది. ‘రవ్వ రవ్వల ఎల్లమ్మ’కు రంగు రంగుల చీర కట్టి, అలంకరించిన రథంపై ఊరేగింపుకు ఎక్కిస్తారు. పసుపు కుంకుమలు చేతబట్టి, పట్టుచీరలు కట్టుకున్న పడుచులు అమ్మకు పూజ చేసి మొక్కులు చెల్లించుకోవడానికి వస్తారు. భక్తులు నెత్తిన బోనమెత్తుకుని బోనాల పండుగ తీరులో వచ్చి నైవేద్యం సమర్పిస్తారు, డప్పు సప్పుళ్లతో దరువేస్తారు.

పూజా స్థలం వివరాలు కూడా పాటలో ఉన్నాయి: గ్రామదేవతతో దగ్గరి సంబంధం ఉన్న వేపాకు మండలతో పందిరి వేస్తారు, అమ్మ మెడలో మల్లెపూల దండలు వేస్తారు, బంగారు చెంబుతో నీళ్లు తెచ్చి స్నానం చేయిస్తారు. ‘సల్లగ చూడమ్మ’, ‘మమ్ము దీవించమ్మ’ అని భక్తులు వేడుకుంటారు. చివరి చరణంలో ‘ఏడు ఊర్ల ఎల్లమ్మ, ఏలిక నీవే’ అని కీర్తించి, ఊరి ప్రజలందరినీ కాపాడమని ప్రార్థిస్తారు. వర్ణనలు, ‘దరువెయ్యరో’, ‘దండమెట్టరో’, ‘పందిరెయ్యరో’ వంటి పిలుపులు కలిసి ఉండటం వల్ల ఇది జాతరలోనే జనమంతా కలిసి పాడుకునే పాటగా అనిపిస్తుంది.
